newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Copper faces roller-coaster week.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Copper faces roller-coaster week.

text.p: Copper prices, which reached six-month peaks of $2,313 a tonne at one stage last week, only to fall away and end Friday at $2,242, are expected to start December in a volatile mood.

In addition to warehouse inventory data on Tuesday and Friday, London Metal Exchange (LME) December traded options will be declared on Wednesday. A key strike will be the $2,600 upside call, where open interest exceeds available LME warehouse stock.
"The only thing you can say is that it will be a bumpy ride with lots of volatility," a senior trader said.

In the middle of last month, copper prices broke out of a range just under $1,900 and just above $2,000. As a result, many upside option positions that had seemed destined to be abandoned are now likely to be exercised.

There are around 6,700 lots of $2,600 calls, equivalent to over 168,000 tonnes of copper. If the December date, currently around $2,383, is at or near $2,600 and these calls are declared a tidal wave of covering could push nearby prices up to $2,800, some said.
If so, there will be a knock-on effect on backwardations, with cash/threes currently at $235. Last week this premium reached $285 as December 16-18 tightness increased sharply.

This period has become critical because of rolling forward of short positions from three, six and even 12 months ago, as well as end-year business. And any positions resulting from December options will be for Dec 18 -- the third Wednesday.
The market will also look at stocks data following last Friday's increase of 2,425 tonnes to 92,475 -- the first rise since early September.
Traders had been expecting stocks to start rising from six-14 year lows, with backwardations sucking in metal.A further 20,000 tonnes could added before the end of the year.
Aluminium, which also reached six-month highs last week when prices traded up to $1,571, has the potential to push higher again as stocks are falling.

"Aluminium is poised to become the LME's flagship metal up to the millenium. There was a welcome drawdown in stocks (last Friday), making a total of 12,400 tonnes for the week," analyst Nick Moore of the Flemings Gloabl Mining Group said.
LME trader Brandeis noted that U.S. aluminium orders had improved markedly over the past few months, with domestic industry orders up almost 17 percent since September.
Japanese demand continues to increase, with shipments of fabricated products reaching record levels during the third quarter.
"This is a very positive scenario that is unfolding," Moore said.
